sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是“99%隐形”。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Morris.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·莫里斯。

sentences.en: I think if you ask somebody on the street, what is camouflage,
sentences.zh: 我想如果你在街上随便问一个人，什么是迷彩，

sentences.en: I believe the most common answer would be to say,
sentences.zh: 我相信最常见的回答会是，

sentences.en: well, it's a figure and it's being hidden by being blended with its background.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是一个物体，它通过与背景融为一体来把自己隐藏起来。

sentences.en: Scientists today call that background matching.
sentences.zh: 现在的科学家把这叫做背景匹配。

sentences.en: I call that high similarity camouflage.
sentences.zh: 我把它叫做高度相似迷彩。

sentences.en: That's Roy Behrens.
sentences.zh: 那是罗伊·贝伦斯。

sentences.en: I'm Roy Behrens and I teach in the Department of Art at the University of Northern Iowa.
sentences.zh: 我是罗伊·贝伦斯，我在北爱荷华大学艺术系教书。

sentences.en: I teach graphic design and the history of design.
sentences.zh: 我教平面设计和设计史。

sentences.en: Behrens is also one of the foremost camouflage experts.
sentences.zh: 贝伦斯也是最重要的迷彩专家之一。

sentences.en: Well, I wouldn't go that far.
sentences.zh: 呃，我可不敢当。

sentences.en: I would.
sentences.zh: 我敢。

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 我就是。

sentences.en: High similarity or blending is just one type of camouflage.
sentences.zh: 高度相似或融合只是迷彩的一种。

sentences.en: It's kind of the boring one.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是最无聊的一种。

sentences.en: But another type of camouflage that you can find both in nature and in military use
sentences.zh: 但你在自然界和军事用途中都能找到的另一种迷彩

sentences.en: is disruptive camouflage.
sentences.zh: 就是破坏性迷彩。

sentences.en: I call it figure disruption.
sentences.zh: 我把它叫做轮廓破坏。

sentences.en: Figure disruption.
sentences.zh: 轮廓破坏。

sentences.en: Figure disruption.
sentences.zh: 轮廓破坏。

sentences.en: Because it breaks up the figure.
sentences.zh: 因为它打碎了物体的轮廓。

sentences.en: It's the opposite of high similarity camouflage.
sentences.zh: 它与高度相似迷彩正好相反。

sentences.en: It's high difference.
sentences.zh: 它是高度差异。

sentences.en: So you're making it very difficult for us to look at the figure
sentences.zh: 所以你让人们很难去观察这个物体

sentences.en: and to see it as only a single continuous thing.
sentences.zh: 并把它看作是一个单一的连续整体。

sentences.en: Interruption.
sentences.zh: 打断。

sentences.en: Figure disruption.
sentences.zh: 轮廓破坏。

sentences.en: Zebra stripes have long been thought to be a form of disruptive camouflage.
sentences.zh: 斑马纹长期以来一直被认为是一种破坏性迷彩。

sentences.en: The stripes make it hard for a predator to distinguish one zebra from another
sentences.zh: 当斑马处于庞大的群落中时，

sentences.en: when the zebras are in a large herd.
sentences.zh: 这些条纹让捕食者很难把一头斑马和另一头区分开来。

sentences.en: The stripes might also make zebras less attractive to blood-sucking horseflies.
sentences.zh: 这些条纹还可能让斑马对吸血的马蝇失去吸引力。

sentences.en: But when it comes to humans, the greatest, most jaw-droppingly spectacular application
sentences.zh: 但说到人类，军事上最伟大、最令人目瞪口呆的破坏性迷彩应用

sentences.en: of disruptive camouflage by the military is razzle-dazzle.
sentences.zh: 就是眩晕迷彩。

sentences.en: Dazzle camouflage strictly applies to ship camouflage.
sentences.zh: 眩晕迷彩严格来说仅适用于舰船迷彩。

sentences.en: And even more strictly, it applies to World War I ship camouflage.
sentences.zh: 更严格地说，它适用于第一次世界大战的舰船迷彩。

sentences.en: And it came about because it was discovered that it's almost impossible to make a ship invisible on the ocean.
sentences.zh: 它的出现是因为人们发现，要让一艘船在海洋上隐形几乎是不可能的。

sentences.en: The horizon is changing in color.
sentences.zh: 地平线的颜色在变。

sentences.en: It's changing in amount of light.
sentences.zh: 光线强弱在变。

sentences.en: So there are all kinds of conditions that make it so a constantly moving ship can't blend into the background of the sea.
sentences.zh: 所以各种条件使得一艘不断移动的船无法融入海洋背景中。

sentences.en: And even if you could make a ship invisible,
sentences.zh: 而且即使你能让一艘船隐形，

sentences.en: you still have smoke coming out of the smokestack, so it's not as if you're hiding the ship at all.
sentences.zh: 烟囱里依然会冒出烟雾，所以这就好像你根本没有隐藏这艘船一样。

sentences.en: So the less heavily armored ships were sitting ducks.
sentences.zh: 因此，那些装甲较薄的船只就成了活靶子。

sentences.en: The crisis came about at the time that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这场危机爆发时，美国

sentences.en: had not yet entered the war.
sentences.zh: 尚未参战。

sentences.en: Remember, this is World War I.
sentences.zh: 记住，这是第一次世界大战。

sentences.en: It was the British ships that were being sunk.
sentences.zh: 当时遭到击沉的是英国船只。

sentences.en: And the German submarines were sinking as many as 50 ships a week.
sentences.zh: 德国潜艇每周击沉多达50艘船。

sentences.en: Many of those ships were merchant ships.
sentences.zh: 其中许多船只都是商船。

sentences.en: And they were bringing supplies to England, which is an island, of course.
sentences.zh: 它们为英国运送物资，当然，英国是一个岛国。

sentences.en: And it really depended on those.
sentences.zh: 它确实非常依赖这些物资。

sentences.en: And then also there was armaments and other things that were being secretly taken there, too.
sentences.zh: 同时还有武器和其他秘密运往那里的东西。

sentences.en: So the design solution was not about invisibility.
sentences.zh: 所以设计的解决方案不是关于隐形。

sentences.en: It was about disruption.
sentences.zh: 而是关于破坏。

sentences.en: A number of artists decided that the best way to avoid getting torpedoed
sentences.zh: 许多艺术家认为，避免被鱼雷击中的最好方法

sentences.en: was not to make the ship invisible, but to make it hard to hit.
sentences.zh: 不是让船隐形，而是让它很难被击中。

sentences.en: That's why these kind of erratic, crazy quilt patterns came about.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么这种不规律的、疯狂的拼布图案会应运而生。

sentences.en: And that's why they were used in that war.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么它们在那场战争中被使用。

sentences.en: It's going to be hard to picture this, but I want you to try.
sentences.zh: 这可能很难想象，但我希望你试一试。

sentences.en: There once was a time when military ships, even U.S.
sentences.zh: 曾几何时，军舰，甚至到这个时候的美国

sentences.en: ships by this point, were painted with,
sentences.zh: 军舰，都被涂上了——

sentences.en: and I quote,
sentences.zh: 我引用一下，

sentences.en: this is from an anonymous article in the New York Times from 1918.
sentences.zh: 这是摘自《纽约时报》1918年的一篇匿名文章。

sentences.en: Any New Yorker will see at anchor or coming in or going out
sentences.zh: 任何纽约人只要看到抛锚、进港或出港的

sentences.en: numerous ships whose painted signs reveal such wild extravagances of form and color
sentences.zh: 无数船只，其涂装展现出如此狂野的形状和色彩的奢华，

sentences.en: as make the landsman open his eyes with amazement and mystification.
sentences.zh: 以至于让内地人惊讶和迷惑得目瞪口呆。

sentences.en: Black and white was very common.
sentences.zh: 黑白相间非常普遍。

sentences.en: They consist of stripes and swirls and kind of arabesque, almost art nouveau shapes.
sentences.zh: 它们由条纹、漩涡以及某种蔓藤花纹、几乎是新艺术运动风格的形状组成。

sentences.en: Blue was used predominantly, especially in the British versions.
sentences.zh: 蓝色被广泛使用，特别是在英国版本中。

sentences.en: But I think you'd be surprised at the range of colors.
sentences.zh: 但我想你会对色彩的范围感到惊讶。

sentences.en: There were reds that were sometimes used and greens and really quite intense oranges.
sentences.zh: 有时会使用红色、绿色以及非常浓烈的橙色。

sentences.en: Another unidentified U.S.
sentences.zh: 另一位未具名的美国

sentences.en: journalist wrote,
sentences.zh: 记者写道，

sentences.en: You should see our fleet.
sentences.zh: 你应该看看我们的舰队。

sentences.en: It's camouflaged so it looks like a flock of seagoing Easter eggs.
sentences.zh: 它被伪装得看起来像一群远洋复活节彩蛋。

sentences.en: During World War I, dazzle ship camouflage was absolutely fascinating to the public.
sentences.zh: 在第一次世界大战期间，眩晕舰船迷彩对公众而言绝对具有迷人的吸引力。

sentences.en: You have to remember that this is happening just a few years after the,
sentences.zh: 你必须记住，这发生在纽约所谓的

sentences.en: what's called the Armory Show in New York.
sentences.zh: 军械库展之后仅仅几年。

sentences.en: It's the first international show of modern art in this country.
sentences.zh: 这是该国第一个现代艺术国际展览。

sentences.en: And it was the introductory show of cubism, futurism, all of those things that people made fun of.
sentences.zh: 它是立体主义、未来主义以及所有那些人们嘲笑的事物的介绍性展览。

sentences.en: And they thought that, you know, that these are really crazy directions for artists to be going into.
sentences.zh: 他们认为，你知道，这些对艺术家来说真的是疯狂的方向。

sentences.en: So that when this happened, people looked at those ships and they said,
sentences.zh: 所以当这件事发生时，人们看着那些船并说道，

sentences.en: Oh, it's a cubist nightmare.
sentences.zh: 哦，这是一场立体主义的噩梦。

sentences.en: It's futurists.
sentences.zh: 这是未来主义者。

sentences.en: They've taken over the world.
sentences.zh: 他们已经接管了世界。

sentences.en: As you can probably guess, there were plenty of people who hated dazzle camouflage.
sentences.zh: 正如你所能猜到的，有很多人讨厌眩晕迷彩。

sentences.en: Traditional Navy men, mostly.
sentences.zh: 主要是传统的海军军官。

sentences.en: They compared it to the clothing that a prostitute would wear.
sentences.zh: 他们把它比作妓女穿的衣服。

sentences.en: And they made fun of it.
sentences.zh: 并且他们取笑它。

sentences.en: Here's how it worked.
sentences.zh: 它是这样运作的。

sentences.en: I can lead you through the steps.
sentences.zh: 我可以带你了解这些步骤。

sentences.en: At the time, torpedoes fired from U-boats were quite slow,
sentences.zh: 当时，从U型潜艇发射的鱼雷相当慢，

sentences.en: maybe taking a couple minutes to reach their target.
sentences.zh: 可能需要几分钟才能到达目标。

sentences.en: So the person firing the torpedo had to lead the target.
sentences.zh: 所以发射鱼雷的人必须提前预判目标。

sentences.en: He had to anticipate where the target ship was going to be when the torpedo arrived.
sentences.zh: 他必须预料当鱼雷到达时目标船只将在哪里。

sentences.en: So he had to calculate how to do that.
sentences.zh: 所以他必须计算如何做到这一点。

sentences.en: And that very much depended on knowing the exact angle it's headed toward.
sentences.zh: 这在很大程度上取决于了解它前进的准确角度。

sentences.en: That's terribly, terribly important.
sentences.zh: 这是非常非常重要的。

sentences.en: And the other thing is that you have to figure out the speed of the ship.
sentences.zh: 另一件事是，你必须算出船的速度。

sentences.en: Because then you'll know how far it can go by the time the torpedo gets there.
sentences.zh: 因为这样你就会知道在鱼雷到达时它能行进多远。

sentences.en: The dazzle camouflage certainly made the ship stand out.
sentences.zh: 眩晕迷彩确实让船非常显眼。

sentences.en: But the bulging shapes and vivid hues also made it difficult to determine the speed and direction of the moving ship.
sentences.zh: 但凹凸不全的形状和鲜艳的色调也让人很难确定移动船只的速度和方向。

sentences.en: It's preying on our assumptions about things looking smaller as they are more distant.
sentences.zh: 它利用了我们的假设，即物体在更远时看起来更小。

sentences.en: So you could paint perspective patterns on a ship that would make it look like it was turning in a different direction.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以在一艘船上画上透视图案，让它看起来像是在朝不同的方向转弯。

sentences.en: When, in fact, you're actually seeing them frontally and they're absolutely flat.
sentences.zh: 而实际上，你看到的是它们的正面，它们是绝对平坦的。

sentences.en: The dazzle patterns broke up the figure so that it could look shorter than it really was.
sentences.zh: 眩晕图案打破了轮廓，使其看起来比实际更短。

sentences.en: Or it could make it hard to tell if there was one ship or multiple ships.
sentences.zh: 或者它可能很难辨别是一艘船还是多艘船。

sentences.en: They even painted fake bow waves on them.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至在船上画了假的船头浪。

sentences.en: And they would paint the fake bow wave either on the front to make it look like the ship was going faster than it was actually going.
sentences.zh: 他们会在前面画上假的船头浪，让船看起来比实际航行得更快。

sentences.en: Because that was one way of calculating that.
sentences.zh: 因为那是计算方法之一。

sentences.en: Or they would paint the bow wave on the back.
sentences.zh: 或者他们会在后面画上船头浪。

sentences.en: And so you would glance at it while you're looking through this periscope.
sentences.zh: 所以当你通过潜望镜观察时扫视它一眼。

sentences.en: You might conclude that, oh, it's going in that direction, not in the other direction.
sentences.zh: 你可能会得出结论，哦，它是在朝那个方向开，而不是朝另一个方向。

sentences.en: So then you surface again to calculate where you're going to shoot.
sentences.zh: 所以你再次浮出水面来计算你要在哪里射击。

sentences.en: And the thing is gone.
sentences.zh: 而那个东西已经不见了。

sentences.en: It's an entirely different direction and location than you imagined.
sentences.zh: 它是一个与你想象的完全不同的方向和位置。

sentences.en: These patterns weren't just slapped on the side of giant ships hoping that they'd be confusing enough to be effective.
sentences.zh: 这些图案不仅仅是拍在巨型船只的侧面，希望它们足够混乱以达到效果。

sentences.en: Camouflors, and that's what they were called,
sentences.zh: 迷彩专家，他们就是这样被称呼的，

sentences.en: the camouflors tested toy models by inviting in experienced submarine captains to peer through periscopes and report what angle they thought the models were pointed.
sentences.zh: 这些迷彩专家通过邀请经验丰富的潜水艇长透过潜望镜窥视并报告他们认为模型指向什么角度来测试玩具模型。

sentences.en: They determined that sometimes on really effectively camouflaged ships, the calculation of the ship captains could be off as much as 55 degrees.
sentences.zh: 他们确定，有时在真正有效伪装的船只上，船长的计算可能会偏差达55度。

sentences.en: Dazzle only had to screw up the torpedo gunner's estimate by 8 degrees for the target ship to effectively avoid a torpedo.
sentences.zh: 眩晕迷彩只需要把鱼雷炮手的估计搞错8度，目标船只就能有效地避开鱼雷。

sentences.en: The theater of war has changed, so camouflage has changed with it.
sentences.zh: 战争的舞台已经改变，所以迷彩也随之改变。

sentences.en: But there is still Dazzle to be found.
sentences.zh: 但仍然可以找到眩晕迷彩的踪迹。

sentences.en: Actually, if you look at military craft today, there is still Dazzle being practiced.
sentences.zh: 事实上，如果你看看今天的军用舰艇，仍然有人在实践眩晕迷彩。

sentences.en: But, of course, the conditions have changed.
sentences.zh: 但是，当然，条件已经改变了。

sentences.en: Just as in World War I, this came out of those particular set of conditions, we have to say, well, those aren't the conditions that we have now,
sentences.zh: 正如在第一次世界大战中，这是从那组特定条件中产生的一样，我们必须说，嗯，那些不是我们现在拥有的条件，

sentences.en: so what would be most effective today?
sentences.zh: 那么今天什么才最有效呢？

sentences.en: If you look at aircraft, it's broken up very often.
sentences.zh: 如果你看飞机，它经常被分割开来。

sentences.en: If you look at ships, some of them are broken up through these geometric patterns.
sentences.zh: 如果你看船只，其中一些通过这些几何图案被分割开来。

sentences.en: If you look at some camouflage uniforms, infantry uniforms around the world, you'll find all kinds of breakup with Dazzle and so forth, or tanks or trucks and so forth.
sentences.zh: 如果你看一些迷彩制服，世界各地的步兵制服，你会发现各种带有眩晕迷彩等的分割，或者坦克或卡车等等。

sentences.en: But I'm sad to report that there are no longer flocks of seagoing Easter eggs.
sentences.zh: 但我很遗憾地报告，再也没有远洋复活节彩蛋群了。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible is produced by me, Roman Mars, and Sam Greenspan.
sentences.zh: “99%隐形”由我和罗曼·马尔斯以及萨姆·格林斯潘制作。

sentences.en: We are a project of 91.7, local public radio KALW in San Francisco, and the American Institute of Architects in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山91.7地方公共广播电台KALW以及旧金山美国建筑师学会的项目。

sentences.en: You can find the show and like the show on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 你可以在Facebook上找到并关注这个节目。

sentences.en: I tweet at Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我在推特上的账号是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: But this week, you absolutely must go to 99percentinvisible.org and look at pictures of Dazzle ships.
sentences.zh: 但本周，你绝对必须访问99percentinvisible.org并查看眩晕舰船的照片。

sentences.en: They are just that amazing.
sentences.zh: 它们就是那么令人惊叹。

sentences.en: You will not believe it.
sentences.zh: 你不会相信的。

sentences.en: All you will do this week is talk about Dazzle ships.
sentences.zh: 你这周唯一会做的事就是谈论眩晕舰船。

sentences.en: I almost guarantee it.
sentences.zh: 我几乎可以向你保证。
